# Requirements-match verdict: block

Reviewed candidate: `f24ed4b2bd1acda323d9ec9a6ae494f30b561bf9`
Base: `f98dcd552fc016441478b4fe15920c9f8ad3f05e`
Lens: requirements match only. One actionable evidence-calibration gap remains; the owner’s goals and five-scenario scope are otherwise preserved.

## Finding

**P2 — Mark the inherited-mutation diagnosis as source review, with its reproduction unexecuted.**

`tasks/1_in-progress/2026-09-25-audit-repository-health-and-next-tasks/next-tasks.md:15` states, “A restack can combine an already committed answer and claim into a synthetic mutation.” The same task’s `design.md:27` calls it “The continuity mutation defect.” Neither states that this audit’s diagnosis came from source review and that the current-checker reproduction has not run. The next-task sentence says a red regression is the first future check, but the new handoff still presents the diagnosis without its evidence limit. This fails the supplied pass criterion: “Source-review-only bug diagnosis is identified as unexecuted.” The older backlog task and the 2026-09-04 decision establish ownership and the previously identified concern; they do not establish a new observed failure at this audit’s candidate.

Before closing this audit, add the explicit evidence boundary to the new next-task/design record: source review identified the inherited-mutation gap; this audit did not execute its reproduction; the existing task first confirms an observed-red case against the current checker and preserves negative controls. No implementation or new task is needed to remedy this finding. Keep the existing canonical action and task identity.

## Requirements I could not break

- The maintenance scope is high-level-first and records-only. The roadmap starts with the confirmed parallel human-agent development goal; the new plan reuses existing continuity, expected-tip publication, coordination, durable-handover and drift actions. It does not reopen the archived classifier design or advance the deferred viewer/adoption goals.
- Mechanical comparison found all 10 goal titles/order, 20 Asked/Confirmed lines, 10 owner text fences, and eight owner-confirmation statements identical between base and candidate.
- The five-scenario child explicitly says it has not started, has seven derived acceptance criteria, preserves the parent task identity, and points to the parent’s original owner request. Its editing, shared state, recovery, dependent-change and combined-integration scenarios map to the five numbered experiments in that request. It requires exact commands/output/Git IDs/environment and an operations manual; missing protection is a gap, never a passing scenario. The roadmap and new plan do not turn unit-suite results or design into operational proof.
- The coordination backlog correction matches the parent design’s rule that missing/stale runtime evidence does not prove a writer stopped. Its restriction of `2_blocked` to agent blockers matches `tasks/AGENTS.md` and the accepted 2026-08-01 human-gating decision.
- All 58 moved files were checked mechanically: files other than worklogs/verification retain exact bytes, and each changed worklog/verification begins with the complete previous bytes. No frozen human queue file, ADR, immutable handover, core code, runtime configuration, dependency, permission, provider setting or principle appears in the changed-path set.
- All seven moved task records retain checked acceptance and their existing queue links. The external-review operation remains explicitly unexecuted; provider and human actions have not been retired by this diff. This lens did not independently re-prove the historical implementations.

## Commands and environment

Read-only review in `/Users/quentinmiao/.codex/worktrees/bbbb/agentfold`, Darwin arm64, Python 3.14.7. `git rev-parse HEAD` returned the exact reviewed candidate above; `git status --short` produced no output.

Commands actually run included:

- `cat tmp/repo-audit/verify-combined.txt` and `sed` ranges over the mechanically composed `verify-roadmap.txt`.
- `git diff --stat f98dcd552fc016441478b4fe15920c9f8ad3f05e..f24ed4b2bd1acda323d9ec9a6ae494f30b561bf9`, `git diff --name-status -M` for that range, and the raw diff for the coordination backlog correction.
- `cat`, `rg`, and `nl -ba` reads of applicable contracts, goals, the new task/plan/design, the parent’s original requirements and cycle design, existing canonical actions, moved task records, and the accepted authority decisions.
- A read-only `python3 -B` script using `git show` compared goal headings, provenance, owner fences, confirmation sentences, exact moved-file bytes and append-only prefixes. Results: all protected goal collections identical; 58 moved files; zero prefix/immutable-byte violations; zero changed protected-source paths.
- `rg -n 'source.review|unexecuted|unverified|not (run|execute|reproduc)|never (run|execut)|reproduc|mutation|combined.*red'` over the new audit/five-scenario tasks and roadmaps checked the claimed evidence boundary.
- `git show -s --format='%H%n%P%n%s' f24ed4b2bd1acda323d9ec9a6ae494f30b561bf9`, `uname -sm`, and `python3 --version` identified the candidate and environment.

Checks not run: tests, reconciler, caches/fixtures, bootstrap, live provider queries, external review, any of the five owner acceptance experiments, or a reproduction of the inherited-mutation bug. I did not read run findings/progress, worker summaries outside the permitted diff packets, or current reviewers’ verdicts. No repository edits were made.

## Revised requirements-match verdict: approve

Reviewed candidate: `5a696f502d4e56f3822f28cb987d2f1b62468735`
Base: `f98dcd552fc016441478b4fe15920c9f8ad3f05e`

The initial evidence-calibration finding is resolved. I could not break the revised candidate against this requirements lens. This approval applies only to the exact revised SHA; the initial verdict above remains part of the record.

The audit’s `design.md` now says, “Source review identified the inherited-mutation concern; this audit did not execute its reproduction.” Its `next-tasks.md` also explicitly says the reproduction was not executed and requires an observed-red regression first. The existing task/action identity and negative-control requirement are preserved.

The additional completion-boundary action is a supported correction rather than invented scope. The retained machine-record task still has its original zero-unscoped-findings acceptance criterion, while its original verification table and full-check output state 38 findings (`verification.md:22` and `:532`). The revised candidate keeps that task in `3_in-review`, adds one reciprocal agent action at `transition:complete task:2026-08-18-fold-the-queue-machine-record`, and preserves both human questions. Its new known-issue record distinguishes the acceptance-evidence mismatch from normal queue validation. Completion now requires real evidence or a separately justified scope disposition; neither a merged implementation nor a green ordinary suite silently satisfies the disputed criterion.

The original owner goals, priority order, provenance, and verbatim text remain unchanged. A repeated read-only comparison of base to revised candidate found all 10 goal headings/order, 20 provenance lines, 10 owner fences, and eight owner-confirmation statements identical. All 53 files moved by the revised candidate retain exact bytes or append-only historical prefixes. The retained machine-record worklog and verification preserve every original byte; its task record differs only in the reciprocal Queue actions field. No frozen human question, ADR, handover, core code, runtime configuration or principle changed. The five-scenario task is byte-identical to the initial reviewed candidate and still requires operational evidence with explicit unverified limits.

Recheck commands used `sed` on `tmp/repo-audit/verify-revised.txt`, the complete raw `git diff f24ed4b2bd1acda323d9ec9a6ae494f30b561bf9..5a696f502d4e56f3822f28cb987d2f1b62468735`, `git diff --name-status -M` and `--numstat` against the original base, `git show` of immutable candidate records, `cat`/`rg` of applicable memory/queue contracts and historical acceptance evidence, and a `python3 -B` byte-comparison script invoking only Git reads. The environment remains the same read-only Darwin arm64 workspace recorded above. The script reported zero immutable/prefix violations and confirmed that the five-scenario task is unchanged.

Checks not run during this recheck: tests, reconciler, new probes, caches/fixtures, bootstrap, provider/network operations, external review, or any five-scenario acceptance experiment. I did not independently rerun the three fold-shape counterexamples; I inspected their appended command/output and the existing historical contradiction. I did not read other reviewers’ verdicts or run findings/progress. The only write was this requested append to my own review report.
